acknowledge.text: Somewhere in the middle. That's a real place to be.
Okay is okay. Not every day needs a big feeling.
Not up, not down. A steady sort of day, perhaps.

understand.text: Okay can mean steady, or it can mean a bit flat or unsure. Many people find it's worth a moment to check which it is today.
Middle-of-the-road days are a lot of life. They can be a good time for small, easy things.

options.title: Which kind of okay?
options.text: Is it a steady okay, or a flat okay? Is anything sitting underneath?
options.why: A closer look can tell you whether today needs rest, a lift, or nothing at all.
options.prompt: What kind of okay is today?

options.title: Add one good thing
options.text: Plan one small thing you'd enjoy later today.
options.why: Something to look forward to, even small, can lift an ordinary day.

options.title: A gentle stretch
options.text: Reach up, roll your shoulders, turn your head slowly side to side.
options.why: A little movement often wakes up a flat feeling.

options.title: Change the scene
options.text: Step outside, or move to a different room for a bit.
options.why: A new view can shift how a day feels.

options.title: Ask someone how they are
options.text: And really listen to the answer.
options.why: Turning towards someone else is often good for both of you.

options.title: A little better than okay
options.text: What would make today a bit better than okay?
options.why: Knowing what lifts an ordinary day can make it easier to choose.
